message.content:
**How to kill VS Code (code.exe) from the command line**

On Windows you can terminate a running program by its image name (`/IM`) or by its process ID (`/PID`).  
For Visual Studio Code the executable is called **code.exe**.

---

### 1. Kill *all* instances of VS Code

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – target the image name `code.exe`.
* `/F` – force termination (equivalent to “End Process” in Task Manager).

If you also want to terminate any child processes that were started by VS Code (e.g., extensions, debugging sessions), add `/T`:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

---

### 2. Kill a specific instance by PID

First find the PID:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

This will list all `code.exe` processes and their PIDs. Then kill the desired one:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <PID_NUMBER> /F
```

Replace `<PID_NUMBER>` with the actual number shown.

---

### 3. Using PowerShell

If you prefer PowerShell, you can do the same with:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or by PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id <PID_NUMBER> -Force
```

---

### 4. Things to keep in mind

| Issue | What to watch out for |
|-------|------------------------|
| **Admin rights** | If VS Code was launched with elevated privileges, you may need to run the command prompt as Administrator. |
| **Multiple windows** | Each window/tab may spawn its own `code.exe` process; the `/IM` command kills all of them. |
| **Unsaved work** | Force‑killing will close VS Code without prompting to save unsaved files. Use with care. |

---

#### Quick cheat‑sheet

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Kill all VS Code windows immediately. |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | Kill VS Code + all child processes. |
| `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` | List all VS Code processes & PIDs. |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent. |

That’s it! Just open a command prompt (or PowerShell) and paste the appropriate line.
